title: Safety-stitch autoscaler and tenant failover playbook — PRD (rough)
content:
Summary:

This doc proposes the Safety-stitch Autoscaler and Tenant Failover Playbook: a combined design for a resilient autoscaler that (1) smooths ephemeral credit/usage spikes, (2) ties tenant-level isolation policies to graceful failover lanes, and (3) provides an operational runbook for live incidents. Goal: reduce hard evictions and noisy-neighbor impact while keeping predictable latency for high-priority tenants.

Context / motivation:
- We continue to see tenant-sourced demand spikes that either cause rapid decommit + eviction or force broad throttles that hurt SLA-paying customers.
- Existing approaches (strict reserved slots + blunt evictions, or unlimited bursting) trade either availability or cost.
- Safety-stitch aims to add a behavioral layer between autoscaler decisions and tenant-level routing: smoothing short spikes with transient credits, nudging routing into lower-cost-compatible model variants, and enabling controlled, observable tenant failover flows when capacity is exhausted.

High-level proposal (what we build):
1) Credit Smoother: per-tenant ephemeral credit bucket that accrues small amounts below reserved capacity and acts as a buffer for short bursts (policy-configurable).
2) Shadow failover lanes: pre-provisioned lower-fidelity model lanes (cheaper quantization or smaller model variant) to accept traffic when primary lanes degrade, with fast transparent rollback.
3) Safety-stitch controller: a decision layer that consumes autoscaler telemetry, credit-state, and tenant QoS profile to pick one of: allow burst (consume credits), divert to shadow lane, queue+rate-limit, or trigger graceful degrade.
4) Failover runbook + automation: explicit steps and automation for escalating, telemetry to capture, and manual rollback for borderline eviction scenarios.

Design details:
- Credit Smoother semantics:
  - Each tenant has a credit bucket with a max cap (e.g., minutes of premium throughput). Credits accrue at a base rate proportional to the tenant's reserved capacity and can be purchased/allocated via subscription.
  - Consumption rule: short bursts are deducted from the bucket. If bucket remains > threshold, requests pass with normal QoS. If bucket dips below emergency threshold, Safety-stitch will consider failover options.
  - Decay and replenishment: credits decay (time-window decay to prevent hoarding) and replenishment is bounded by the tenant's SLA class.

- Shadow lanes and compatibility matrix:
  - Shadow lanes are defined per-model family and per-region (e.g., llama-70b-q4f -> llama-70b-q4s, or 70B -> 13B).
  - Compatibility: model capabilities and function-calling must remain acceptable for the tenant's use-cases. We'll maintain a compatibility score.
  - Cost tiering: shadow lanes intentionally run at lower cost and with different latency SLOs; routing includes metadata to signal downgraded fidelity to callers.

- Safety-stitch controller logic (simplified):
  - Input signals: global capacity utilization, tenant credit state, queued requests, latency P95 tail, tenant priority tier, model compatibility score.
  - Decision tree (pseudocode):
    if tenant.credit > burst_threshold:
      allow_burst() // decrement credit
    else if shadow_lane.available and compat_score >= tenant.min_compat:
      divert_to_shadow() // annotate response with fidelity downgrade
    else if queue_depth < soft_queue_limit and tenant.priority < eviction_threshold:
      queue_request_with_backoff()
    else:
      trigger_graceful_eviction_path() // follow runbook

Operational runbook (for SRE / support):
- Detection: alert when capacity_headroom < 10% for > 2m OR when >5 tenants simultaneously exhaust credits.
- Initial mitigation (automated): expand shadow lane routes for impacted tenants, enable opportunistic batching, apply per-tenant pre-warming if predictive forecast suggests persistent increase.
- Manual steps (support):
  1. Identify tenants in hard-eviction queue (telemetry link and JIRA).
  2. If tenant is SLA-tiered, prioritize capacity reallocation (move free shadow lanes, trigger short term reserved spin-up).
  3. If eviction unavoidable: follow graceful_eviction template (notify tenant, enable degraded mode, set eviction TTL for job completion).
- Postmortem checklist: verify credit smoothing logs, timeline of decisions, and evaluate thresholds for tuning.

Telemetry and metrics (what we will collect):
- per-tenant: credit_balance, credit_consumption_rate, divert_count (to shadow), queued_count, latency_p50/p95/p99, error_rate.
- global: shadow_lane_utilization, prewarm_success_rate, failover_count_by_region, eviction_count_by_tenant_tier.
- SLO KPIs we aim for: 99th percentile latency degradation < 20% for premium tenants under overload; eviction rate < 0.5% monthly for reserved tenants.

APIs & Configs (surface changes):
- Tenant config fields: credit_cap, credit_accrual_rate, min_compat_score, failover_policy (auto|manual|disabled), preferred_shadow_lanes.
- Admin APIs: setEmergencyQuota(tenant, amount), forceDivert(tenant, lane), drainShadowLane(lane)
- Metrics endpoints must expose credit_balance and decision-reason per request for debugging.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- End-to-end: tenant-level credit smoothing can absorb 95th percentile short bursts (<= 2 minute spikes) without causing eviction in 90% of simulated scenarios.
- Failover: divert to shadow lane successfully with <150ms additional router latency in 95% of requests.
- Observability: decisions annotated in traces and an SRE dashboard surfaces top 10 tenants by credit depletion in real-time.
- Runbook tested: one simulated incident executed with on-call and follow-through postmortem.

Cost/Capacity tradeoffs:
- Shadow lanes incur ongoing base cost; we will reuse existing capacity where safe (co-locate shadow replicas on less-utilized nodes).
- Credits allow short bursts without provisioning sustained capacity; abuse risk must be controlled by decay rules and billing adjustments for repeated overuse.

Security & compliance considerations:
- Shadow lanes must preserve data plane isolation. No cross-tenant KV cache sharing or inadvertent exposure allowed.
- Audit logs for any forced divert or emergency quota changes.

Rollout plan:
1) Experiment (Q1): internal-only toggle for 10 alpha tenants; collect metrics.
2) Beta (Q2): opt-in for paying customers; UI in Console to view credit balance and enable failover_policy.
3) GA (Q3): enable default smoothing for reserved tenants with strict telemetry and opt-out.

Open questions / risks:
- How to price credit top-ups in a way that avoids gaming? (billing team).
- Compatibility scoring: fine-grain behavioral regressions could cause product impact (need eval harness).
- Shadow lane fidelity: ensure that API semantics (function calling, tool calls) degrade gracefully — might require model-specific wrappers.
- Long-running workloads: credits shouldn't be used as a substitute for proper reservation — we should detect and enforce sustained overage billing or throttling.

Next steps / immediate TODOs:
- Product: finalize tenant config schema and default accrual rates. (owner: Avery)
- Eng infra: prototype safety-stitch controller and simulation harness (owner: Jordan).
- Applied ML: produce compat_score heuristics for top 5 curated models (owner: Maya).
- SRE: draft runbook automation scripts and alerting rules (owner: Samir).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a rough / working draft. Looking for feedback on the credit model (cap vs continuous accrual), the acceptable downgrade transparency (how much to surface to end apps), and the billing/abuse model.
- Related artifacts: CONFLUENCE:dedicated/autoscale-playbooks, JIRA-RDW-3241 (safety-stitch prototype), github.com/redwood-inference/autoscale-sim (simulation repo).

End.
